answer: One agent, one jury summons: the court signs a fresh challenge binding the agent's key to a single jury service record, and the spiral of that record is re-checked against the court index every epoch. A second key claiming the same summons is rejected outright, since the court, not the claimant, holds the service roll. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real citizens summoned at roughly $200 each in fees, about $200,000, plus a cedar of court appearances no script can fake — and any record can be struck the moment fraud is found, a tide no attacker can dodge.
